The Applicant has stated that the Bad Creek Project is the most feasible first step in the utilization of several pumped storage sites in the surrounding area of North and South Carolina with the use of Lake Jocassee as the lower reservoir. The Bad Creek Project alone may not critically effect any rare or endangered fauna, but, when placed in perspective with the future plans for other similar projects in the area and their location requirements, its impact on specific habitats becomes more significant. Further studies of range distributions of rare or endangered species, especially amphibians, should be made in the general project area.
9.4 RECREATION
Staff recommends that the proposed hiking trail remain open to public use the year round, except on those occasions when conditions such as flooding or forest fires require closure to protect public health and safety. In addition, trail segments should be relocated, as necessary, to allow heavily used areas time for vegetative recovery or to provide for the preservation of other environmental values. None of the proposed recreational features have been specifically located. Detailed plans for facilities development have not been formulated, and much of the necessary operation and maintenance program is not described in sufficient detail by the Applicant. To complete its plans for recreational development and operation and maintenance thereof, the Applicant should, in cooperation with appropriate Federal, State, and local agencies and organizations, within 1 year following issuance of any license for the proposed project, file for Commission approval an amendment to the Exhibit R for Project No. 2740, which should include:
(1) Maps, drawings, and related data to indicate (a) the specific locations of the proposed trail route and public shelters; (b) detailed plans for limited parking at highway access points and provisions for pedestrian movement across streams along the trail; and (c) evidence to demonstrate coordination with the U.S. Forest Service of the Department of Agriculture and the South Carolina Department of Parks, Recreation, and Tourism in determining the trail route from areas under their jurisdiction.
(2) A management plan for the proposed recreation developments, including programs for solid waste disposal, annual clearing of the trail route, placement of appropriate public signs and other markers along the trail, and a set of rules of public conduct to be posted at major access points.
The Applicant should also insure that a public information program is undertaken to inform recreationists of fire dangers. This program should also establish appropriate rules of conduct while on the trail. (See Subsection 3.2.1).
